While isavuconazonium sulfate is approved for the treatment of invasive 
mucormycosis, posaconazole has not been FDA approved for this 
indication. Isavuconazonium sulfate and posaconazole can also be 
considered as maintenance therapy for mucormycosis following control of 
infection with an amphotericin B formulation and/or surgical debridement. 

sinusitis each favored a diagnosis of mucormycosis.511 However, some 
transplant centers reported an increased frequency of mucormycosis that 
pre-dated the availability of voriconazole,626,627 a finding that likely reflects 
a greater proportion of patients with severe host defense impairment. 
Mucormycosis typically manifests as rhinocerebral or pulmonary disease. 
Histopathology showing broad aseptate or hyposeptate hyphae with 
90-degree branching is suggestive of mucormycosis, although culture is 
required for confirmation. 

Fusarium species630-632 and Scedosporium species have emerged as 
important causes of invasive fungal infection-related mortality in leukemia 
and in allogeneic HCT recipients at some centers.627,633,634 The likelihood 
of infection by a Fusarium species is substantially increased by the 
presence of disseminated cutaneous lesions and isolation of a mold from 
blood culture.630 Therapy for invasive fusariosis generally involves 
voriconazole,635 posaconazole,622 or a lipid formulation of amphotericin 
B.636 Scedosporium species are resistant to amphotericin B; therapy 
generally involves itraconazole, voriconazole, or posaconazole.637,638 An 
infectious disease consultation is advised in all cases of invasive mold 
infections, particularly for cases involving uncommon and resistant molds. 

Early Diagnosis of Invasive Mold Infections 

To date, there have been no positive results from randomized studies for 
treatment of mucormycosis and other uncommon invasive mold infections. 
Therefore, recommendations for therapy are based on a limited number of 
patients from retrospective analyses, data registries, and open-label trials 
for refractory infections. Treatment of mucormycosis involves amphotericin 
B (a lipid formulation is advised over AmB-D to reduce the chance of 
nephrotoxicity) plus early and aggressive surgical debridement, when 
feasible. A gap in knowledge exists regarding optimal dosing of 
amphotericin B lipid formulations for invasive non-Aspergillus mold 
infections; an initial dose of 5 mg/kg/day is commonly used. 
Isavuconazonium sulfate and posaconazole have shown promising results 
as therapy in mucormycosis refractory to or intolerant of amphotericin B 
formulations and may be considered for these patients.619,628,629 Data from 
an open-label, single-arm, case-control study showed that 
isavuconazonium sulfate had activity against rare fungi, including 
mucormycosis, compared to matched controls treated with amphotericin 
B-based treatment (crude all-cause mortality of 33% vs. 39%; 95% CIs, 
14.6–57.0% and 22.9–57.9%, respectively).629 Ninety-five percent of 
patients treated with isavuconazonium sulfate had one or more adverse 
events during treatment, most commonly GI disorders (see Toxicities and 
Drug-Drug Interactions of Azoles for more information on safety). 

The frequency and diversity of invasive fungal pathogens have increased, 
and effectively treating these pathogens remains a major challenge. CT 
scanning of the chest may facilitate early detection of aspergillosis and 
other filamentous fungi.639,640 A CT scan may show peripheral or 
subpleural nodules that are not apparent on plain chest radiographs. The 
“halo sign” is a characteristic, but not pathognomonic, early chest CT 
feature of angioinvasive organisms.537 The hazy alveolar infiltrates 
surrounding the central nodule or region of consolidation appear to 
correspond to regions of hemorrhage and are highly suggestive of 
invasive mold disease, aspergillosis being the most common. The Panel 
recommends a chest CT scan in patients with 10 to 14 days of 
neutropenia and with persistent or recurrent fever of unknown origin that is 
unresponsive to empiric antibacterial agents. A chest CT scan may be

level,498 and more research is required. Currently, the evidence is 
inadequate to recommend any of these methods as a surveillance tool in 
patients who are asymptomatic immunocompromised or in patients with 
neutropenic fever alone. 

COVID-19 Infection in Patients with Cancer 

Studies differ regarding whether serum galactomannan is a useful 
surveillance tool in asymptomatic patients at high risk for mold infections 
and in patients with persistent neutropenic fever of unknown etiology. In 
one study, prospective serial monitoring of galactomannan antigenemia in 
allogeneic HCT recipients yielded positive and negative predictive values 
of 94.4% and 98.8%, respectively, and antigenemia preceded radiographic 
findings by >1 week in 80% of cases of invasive aspergillosis.641 In 
another study, the sensitivity was only 64.5% in cases of definite invasive 
aspergillosis.546 The PPV was poor when serum galactomannan was used 
as a surveillance tool in patients with persistent neutropenic fever 
(PPV = 7.1%) and in HCT (mostly autologous) recipients (PPV = 10%); the 
negative predictive value was 100% in both groups.546 

Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by severe acute 
respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) can cause increased 
disease severity and mortality in patients with active cancer compared to 
healthy individuals. Patients with cancer who are immunocompromised, 
undergoing chemotherapy, older in age, or having other medical 
conditions are at an increased risk for severe COVID-19. Moreover, 
patients with hematologic malignancies may be at higher risk of prolonged 
infection and death from COVID-19 than patients with solid tumors. The 
CDC provides a comprehensive list of recommendations on testing for 
SARS-CoV-2 and managing COVID-19 and cancer-directed therapies in 
people with concurrent cancer and COVID-19. For a summary of NCCN 
recommendations, see Management of Concurrent COVID-19 and Cancer 
in Patients and General Recommendations for Vaccination in Patients with 
Cancer in the algorithm. 

Summary 

Odabasi et al540 evaluated the beta-glucan assay as an early diagnostic 
marker for invasive fungal infections in patients with acute leukemia or 
MDS receiving antifungal prophylaxis.540 At least one serum sample was 
positive at a median of 10 days before the clinical diagnosis in all patients 
with a proven or probable invasive fungal infection, including candidiasis, 
fusariosis, trichosporonosis, and aspergillosis. The negative predictive 
value was 100%, and the specificity of the test was 90% for a single 
positive test result and at least 96% for two or more sequential positive 
results.540 The experience of the beta-glucan assay in HCT recipients is 
limited and requires additional study. 

Substantial progress has been made in the prevention and treatment of 
infectious complications associated with neutropenia and IST in patients 
with cancer. Certain populations of patients are at increased risk for 
developing infectious complications during the course of their disease and 
cancer treatment. Infectious complications remain an important cause of 
morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing anti-tumor therapy. The 
extent of infectious risk is highly dependent on an individual patient’s 
underlying malignancy, degree of neutropenia, past history of infections 
and exposure to pathogens, treatment with myelosuppressive regimens, 

Although valuable as diagnostic adjuncts to support a diagnosis of 
probable invasive aspergillosis in patients with compatible host factors, 
clinical findings, and radiologic findings642 (see Initial Clinical Presentation 
for Lung Infiltrates: Evaluation in the algorithm), the value of these 
laboratory markers as surveillance tools for invasive fungal infections is 
controversial. Use of surveillance markers as a trigger for additional

pages.text:
categorization and recommended strategies for prevention of infections in 
patient populations at high risk, and recommendations for empiric therapy, 
evaluation, follow-up, and monitoring in patients with signs and/or 
symptoms of infections. Individualized risk evaluation for infections, 
incorporation of preventive measures, and prompt identification and 
treatment of active infections are essential components of the overall 
spectrum of care in cancer management, and can contribute to optimizing 
treatment outcomes in patients with cancer. 

and the overall status of immune function in the patient. It is therefore 
imperative that patients be evaluated individually for risk of infection in 
order to minimize the occurrence of infection-related complications. 
Preventive measures for infection management in patients with cancer 
include routine surveillance to monitor for early laboratory indications of 
infection (especially in the context of viral reactivations) and the 
appropriate use of prophylaxis and/or preemptive therapy with 
antimicrobial agents in patient groups who are at high risk. It is important 
to note that upfront prophylaxis is not necessary in all patients with cancer; 
prophylactic measures should only be used in patients at high risk for 
specific pathogens during the high-risk period in order to avoid the 
emergence of resistant pathogens. 

The development of antipseudomonal beta-lactam agents and the routine 
use of empiric antimicrobial therapy at the onset of neutropenic fever have 
contributed to reductions in mortality from bacterial infections. With more 
patients undergoing treatment with potent cytotoxic regimens and 
receiving allogeneic HCT, opportunistic viral and fungal infections have 
become important causes of mortality in these patients. In addition, the 
increasing prevalence of antibiotic-resistant pathogens is a challenge. 
Infection control should not only rely on anti-infective prophylaxis but 
should continue to incorporate standard infection control measures (eg, 
careful hand-washing by health care professionals). When selecting 
antimicrobial agents for prophylaxis and/or preemptive therapy, 
consideration should be given to the local susceptibility and resistance 
patterns of pathogens. 

In summary, prevention and treatment of infections in patients with cancer 
is a complex and continuously evolving field. However, these advances in 
treatment have only further emphasized the need for multidisciplinary 
care. The NCCN Guidelines for Prevention and Treatment of 
Cancer-Related Infections aim to provide an overview of the risk

nodes.text: RECOMMENDATION: • Adults with anatomic or functional asplenia, persistent complement component deficiency, or on complement inhibitor (eg, eculizumab, ravulizumab) should receive meningococcal vaccination. • The 2-dose primary series for meningococcal conjugate vaccine, quadrivalent (MenACWY) should be administered at least 8 weeks apart with 1 booster dose every 5 years if risk remains. These same patients should also receive vaccination for serogroup B with 1 booster dose 1 year after the primary series and every 2–3 years if risk remains. • A combination of meningococcal pentavalent (ACWY and B) vaccine is available and can be considered as an alternate regimen.

nodes.text: RECOMMENDATION: • The administration of RZV is recommended for adult patients aged ≥50 years and those ≥18 years who are at increased risk for herpes zoster (HZ). The RZV vaccine is given in 2 doses ≥2 to 6 months apart. For adults who are at risk and ≥18 years of age, a second dose can be given 1–2 months after the first dose if they will benefit from a shorter vaccination schedule. For patients who have previously received the live-attenuated zoster vaccine live (ZVL), RZV should be given at least 2 months after the last ZVL dose.

TABLE 1: CONSIDERATIONS FOR CANCER-DIRECTED THERAPY IN PATIENTS WITH SIGNIFICANT EXPOSURE TO SARS-COV-2 • The exact risk of viral transmission after significant exposure to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is unknown and depends upon many variables (eg, symptoms of infected person, duration and proximity of contact, room ventilation, host susceptibility, viral variant). Household contacts pose the highest risk of SARS-CoV-2 transmission. •  If viral transmission occurs to the patient, the upper bound of COVID-19 incubation period is 14 days. • The duration of cancer-directed therapy delay depends on the type and status of malignancy and risk of cancer relapse and progression as a result of delaying therapy. If cancer-directed therapy is urgently required due to uncontrolled cancer, it should be administered at the judgment of the oncologist.

nodes.text: • The heterogeneity of cancers, the complexity and number of different cancer treatment regimens, and variability in the COVID-19 clinical course among patients preclude a single management approach of COVID-19 in all patients with cancer. • Treatment recommendations for COVID-19 among patients with cancer are largely similar to those without cancer (see Table 2); however, several new therapies have become available that demonstrate corresponding benefits for patients with cancer and/or other risk factors for more severe disease. • Table 3 lists currently available COVID-19 treatment options, dosing, and clinical indications. • Comprehensive information on COVID-19–based testing, infection control measures, and evidence-based data for current treatment recommendations can be accessed at: Infectious Disease Society of America, COVID-19 Guidelines. • For unresolved COVID-19, ID consult is recommended.

nodes.text: Preferred • Nirmatrelvir/ ritonavir • Remdesivir Other • Molnupiravir • High-titer COVID-19 convalescent plasma
lines: Preferred • Nirmatrelvir/ ritonavir • Remdesivir Other • Molnupiravir • High-titer COVID-19 convalescent plasma
notes: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir is the favored oral treatment for outpatients with mild to moderate COVID-19 symptoms who are at highest risk of progressing to severe disease and who do not have adverse drug-drug interactions with ritonavir. • Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir use has been shown to reduce risk of hospitalization and death by up to 88%. • Must review potential drug interactions with ritonavir before use. • IV remdesivir is favored when oral nirmatrelvir/ritonavir is not available or suitable because of adverse drug interactions. • 3-day course IV remdesivir has been shown to reduce the risk of hospitalization and death by up to 87%. • Requires IV administration in an infusion center, emergency department, or outpatient clinic; may limit feasibility in outpatient setting. • Oral molnupiravir has decreased efficacy for reducing hospitalization and death (30%) compared with other treatment options, and concerns exist for potential mutagenicity in animal studies. • It is unclear if molnupiravir is a teratogen; however, it is not recommended for use in patients who are pregnant. • Please see Table 3 for recommendations regarding the use of contraception. • High-titer COVID-19 convalescent plasma is under evaluation in the outpatient setting and has been shown to reduce outpatient hospitalizations by >50%. • High-titer COVID-19 convalescent plasma against prevalent circulating viral variants may not be uniformly available and requires transfusion capacity by a local center. • Post-treatment recurrence of symptoms should be treated as a new possible infection with an appropriate evaluation.

The benefit of adding IV remdesivir to dexamethasone in patients who require mechanical ventilation or extracorporeal mechanical oxygenation (ECMO) is unclear, although completion of 5 days of remdesivir is favored if already started before admission to intensive care unit (ICU). • A second immunomodulatory agent (eg, IL-6 inhibitor, JAK inhibitor) is often added for patients with rapidly or progressively declining oxygen saturation (SpO). Use of IL-6 inhibitor and JAK inhibitor is generally avoided in combination, in patients with uncontrolled active infection (bacterial, fungal, mycobacterial, or non-SARS-CoV-2 viral), or in patients with significant concurrent immunosuppression (eg, neutropenia, antineoplastic chemotherapy). Further details of immunomodulatory therapeutic options and indications for patients with moderate to severe COVID-19 are available on the IDSA COVID-19 website. • Additional information for COVID-19 convalescent plasma use is available at: https://covid-convalescentplasma-tbi-calc.org.

notes: • There are no uniform treatment recommendations, but clinical investigational approaches include use of: High-titer COVID-19 convalescent plasma • To determine potential benefit of COVID-19 convalescent plasma, some providers (via clinical investigational approach) will first check: SARS-CoV-2 antibodies to nucleocapsid antigens to confirm lack of adequate humoral response post-infection Viral load burden by PCR after ID consult • Consider avoiding molnupiravir due to concerns for risk of producing escape viral mutants.

• Clinical significance and role for supplemental therapy remain unclear. • SARS-CoV-2 reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) testing does not distinguish replication-competent and infectious virus (eg, growth in cell-line culture) from inactive virus. In a prior review of 28 studies, the pooled median duration of RNA shedding from respiratory sources was 18.4 days with wide heterogeneity (range, 1–63 days) and relatively little difference based on disease severity. Prolonged SARS-CoV-2 detection of replication of the competent virus (>100 days) has been reported in patients who are immunocompromised and has often been associated with a weak or absent antibody response to the virus. • Clinical decisions can be influenced by viral load interpretation (PCR Ct), patient immunologic status, cancer response/lack of response to current therapeutics, etc.

• Monoclonal antibodies have become available, however, due to variant mutations these agents lose activity over time. For pre-exposure prophylaxis, refer to guidance from IDSA or FDA on whether there may be an available monoclonal antibody for this indication.

neutrophils_x10e9_l.definition: Absolute neutrophil count at the time of the case (500 cells/mcL = 0.5 x10^9/l).

anticipated_neutropenia_days.definition: Anticipated duration of neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count below the guideline threshold) stated in the case.

months_since_transplant.definition: Months elapsed since the most recent hematopoietic cell transplant.

mascc_score.definition: MASCC Risk-Index Score for the febrile episode.

cisne_score.definition: CISNE score for the febrile episode.

aminotransferase_multiple_of_uln.definition: Aminotransferase (AST or ALT) value expressed as a multiple of the upper limit of normal.

days_since_symptom_onset.definition: Days elapsed since symptom onset of the current COVID-19 illness.

primary_disease.definition: Primary malignancy or disease category of the patient.

hct_type.definition: Hematopoietic cell transplant received. Cord blood transplant is recorded as allogeneic_or_cord_blood.

cmv_igg_status.definition: CMV IgG serostatus of the patient.

on_alemtuzumab.definition: Patient is receiving or has received alemtuzumab therapy.

on_purine_analog_therapy.definition: Patient is receiving purine analog therapy (fludarabine, clofarabine, nelarabine, cladribine).

on_t_cell_depleting_agent.definition: Patient is receiving a T-cell-depleting agent other than purine analogs or alemtuzumab.

on_proteasome_inhibitor.definition: Patient is receiving a proteasome inhibitor.

on_cellular_immunotherapy.definition: Patient is receiving a cellular immunotherapy (CAR T-cell, TCR or TIL therapy).

on_immune_or_targeted_treatment.definition: Patient is receiving a select immune or targeted treatment (the INF-A list is not in the input; a clinician judgement based on the case).

on_standard_chemo_solid_tumor.definition: Patient is receiving standard chemotherapy for a solid tumor.

on_prolonged_corticosteroids_or_temozolo.definition: Patient is on prolonged corticosteroids or receiving temozolomide with or without radiation therapy.

receiving_immunosuppressive_therapy.definition: Patient is currently receiving immunosuppressive therapy (IST).

gvhd_requiring_therapy.definition: Patient has graft-versus-host disease that requires therapy.

gvhd_requires_ist_escalation.definition: Graft-versus-host disease requires significant escalation of immunosuppressive therapy.

hcv_antibody_positive.definition: HCV antibody screening result is positive.

hcv_rna_detected.definition: HCV viral load is positive (RNA detected).

cmv_prophylaxis_selected.definition: Clinician has selected CMV prophylaxis rather than preemptive monitoring (a clinician choice, not a case fact).

cmv_viremia_detected.definition: Patient has laboratory markers of CMV viremia (CMV DNA or antigen detected).

cmv_asymptomatic.definition: Patient is asymptomatic for CMV disease.

fever_per_guideline_definition.definition: The case states a fever episode meeting the FEV-1 fever definition.

inpatient_at_fever_onset.definition: Patient was an inpatient at the time fever developed.

acute_comorbid_illness_requires_inpatien.definition: Patient has an acute comorbid illness that independently indicates inpatient treatment or close observation.

significant_medical_comorbidity_or_clini.definition: Patient has significant medical comorbidity or is clinically unstable.

renal_insufficiency_present.definition: Patient has renal insufficiency as stated in the case.

prior_quinolone_prophylaxis.definition: Patient received quinolone prophylaxis before the febrile episode.

prior_antibiotic_anaphylaxis.definition: The case states a prior anaphylactic reaction to an antibiotic. Raw input for high_anaphylaxis_risk.

mdro_colonization_or_prior_infection.definition: Patient is colonized with or has prior infection with a multidrug-resistant organism.

home_iv_therapy_feasible.definition: Intravenous antibiotics at home are feasible for this patient (a clinician judgement).

clinically_stable_or_improving.definition: Patient is clinically stable or improving.

persistently_febrile_stable.definition: Patient remains febrile but is otherwise clinically stable.

nausea_or_vomiting.definition: Patient has nausea or vomiting. Used in the oral antibiotic criteria (FEV-4 footnote).

able_to_tolerate_oral_medications.definition: Patient is able to tolerate oral medications. Used in the oral antibiotic criteria (FEV-4 footnote).

cellulitis_or_skin_soft_tissue_infection.definition: Patient has cellulitis or a skin and soft tissue infection.

vesicular_lesions.definition: Patient has vesicular lesions (mucosal or skin).

disseminated_papules_or_lesions.definition: Patient has disseminated papules or other lesions.

cns_symptoms.definition: Patient has central nervous system symptoms.

vad_present.definition: Patient has a vascular access device (VAD).

vad_site_inflammation.definition: VAD entry site or surrounding area is inflamed.

vad_tunnel_port_pocket_infection_or_sept.definition: VAD has a tunnel infection, port pocket infection or septic phlebitis.

cdi_confirmed.definition: Clostridioides difficile infection is confirmed by testing.

other_cause_of_diarrhea_identified.definition: C. difficile testing is negative or another cause of diarrhea has been identified.

other_medical_cause_of_diarrhea_identifi.definition: Another medical cause of diarrhea has been identified (for example neutropenic enterocolitis or a laxative or tube-feed effect).

necrotizing_oral_ulceration.definition: Patient has necrotizing ulceration of the mouth or mucosal membrane.

sinus_nasal_involvement.definition: Sinus or nasal involvement is present.

significant_sars_cov2_exposure.definition: Patient has had a significant exposure to SARS-CoV-2.

cancer_therapy_urgently_required.criteria: If cancer-directed therapy is urgently required due to uncontrolled cancer
cancer_therapy_urgently_required.definition: Cancer-directed therapy is urgently required because the cancer is uncontrolled (a clinician judgement).

persistent_symptomatic_covid.definition: Patient has persistent symptomatic COVID-19 infection.

persistent_asymptomatic_positive_test.definition: Patient has persistent asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2-positive testing.

pre_exposure_prophylaxis_indicated.definition: Pre-exposure prophylaxis against SARS-CoV-2 is indicated (a clinician judgement).

nirmatrelvir_available.definition: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir is available for this patient.

remdesivir_available.definition: Remdesivir is available for this patient.

prolonged_neutropenia_present.definition: The case states prolonged neutropenia. Risk factor for COVID-19 progression (COV-3 box).

t_cell_deficiency_present.definition: The case states T-cell deficiency (lymphopenia) or dysfunction. Risk factor for COVID-19 progression (COV-3 box).

tumor_pulmonary_involvement.definition: The case states tumor involvement of the lung. Risk factor for COVID-19 progression (COV-3 box).

pregnant_or_may_become_pregnant.definition: Patient is pregnant or may become pregnant.

vaccination_general_indicated.definition: Clinician judges general vaccination indicated (INF-7 VACCINATION: General box; the guideline gives no criteria).

influenza_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges influenza vaccination indicated (INF-7 VACCINATION: Influenza and INF-8 Influenza (injectable) boxes; the guideline gives no criteria).

covid19_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges COVID-19 vaccination indicated (INF-7 and INF-8 COVID-19 boxes; the guideline gives no criteria).

pneumococcal_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges pneumococcal vaccination indicated (INF-7 and INF-8 pneumococcal boxes; the guideline gives no criteria).

meningococcal_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges meningococcal vaccination indicated (INF-7 meningococcal and INF-8 ACWY boxes; the guideline gives no criteria).

hpv_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges HPV vaccination indicated (INF-7 HPV and INF-8 HPV boxes; the guideline gives no criteria).

recombinant_zoster_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges recombinant zoster vaccination indicated (INF-7 RZV and INF-8 recombinant zoster boxes; the guideline gives no criteria).

tdap_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges Tdap vaccination indicated (INF-7 Tdap and INF-8 Tdap boxes; the guideline gives no criteria).

rsv_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges respiratory syncytial virus vaccination indicated (INF-7 RSV box; the guideline gives no criteria).

travel_or_other_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges travel or other vaccination indicated (INF-7 Travel and other vaccines box; the guideline gives no criteria).

hib_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccination indicated (INF-8 Hib box; the guideline gives no criteria).

hepatitis_a_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges hepatitis A vaccination indicated (INF-8 Hep A box; the guideline gives no criteria).

hepatitis_b_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges hepatitis B vaccination indicated (INF-8 Hep B box; the guideline gives no criteria).

inactivated_polio_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges inactivated polio vaccination indicated (INF-8 inactivated polio box; the guideline gives no criteria).

mmr_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges measles/mumps/rubella vaccination indicated (INF-8 live vaccine MMR box; the guideline gives no criteria).

varicella_vaccine_indicated.definition: Clinician judges varicella vaccination indicated (INF-8 live vaccine varicella box; the guideline gives no criteria).

infection_risk_overall.definition: Overall infection risk category for antimicrobial prophylaxis (INF-1).

antifungal_prophylaxis_context.definition: Patient context for considering antifungal prophylaxis (INF-2). Rules are ordered by the boxes listed.

hsv_vzv_prophylaxis_category.definition: Risk category for HSV and VZV reactivation prophylaxis (INF-3). Most specific category first.

cmv_high_risk.definition: Patient is high risk for CMV (INF-4): allogeneic HCT recipient who is CMV IgG seropositive with GVHD requiring therapy, or receiving alemtuzumab.

cmv_allo_seropositive_gvhd_therapy.definition: Allogeneic HCT recipient, CMV IgG seropositive, with GVHD requiring therapy (INF-4 box). Contains no alemtuzumab condition.

cmv_preemptive_therapy_criteria.definition: Preemptive therapy criteria (INF-4 footnote): patient is asymptomatic with laboratory markers of viremia.

pjp_post_transplant_window.definition: Patient is 3 to 6 months after transplant (INF-6 timing box).

hcv_active_infection.definition: HCV antibody positive with a positive viral load (INF-5).

febrile_neutropenia.definition: Fever meeting the FEV-1 definition together with neutropenia (ANC at or below 0.5 x10^9/l, or at or below 1.0 with a predicted decline to at or below 0.5 over 48 hours).

fever_risk_group.definition: Risk group for a febrile neutropenic episode (FEV-2). High risk if any high-risk factor is present; low risk if none is present and the low-risk features hold. Otherwise undetermined.

antibiotic_route.definition: Initial antibiotic route (FEV-5). Oral options are considered only for low-risk patients without prior quinolone prophylaxis.

oral_antibiotic_criteria_met.definition: Criteria for oral antibiotics (FEV-4 footnote): no nausea or vomiting, patient able to tolerate oral medications, and patient not on prior fluoroquinolone prophylaxis.

iv_combination_consider.definition: IV combination therapy could be considered (FEV-5): resistance is suspected or the patient has MDRO colonization or prior infection.

high_anaphylaxis_risk.criteria_source: external: unnamed standard definition (box states no criteria; flagged for review)
high_anaphylaxis_risk.definition: High risk of anaphylaxis to antibiotics (FEV-5). The box states no criteria; the standard published definition used here is a prior anaphylactic reaction to an antibiotic, taken from the case fact prior_antibiotic_anaphylaxis.

allergy_consult_consider.definition: Consider infectious diseases or allergy consultation because of high risk of anaphylaxis (FEV-5).

fever_management_branch.definition: Management branch for a patient with fever on treatment (FEV-11 and FEV-12).

fever_unknown_origin_anc_branch.definition: Neutrophil branch for fever resolved with unknown origin (FEV-11).

cdi_negative_or_other_cause_from_finding.definition: C. difficile testing is negative or another cause of diarrhea has been identified (FEV-7 CDI negative/other cause box). Any one of the two findings is sufficient.

covid_exposure_workup.definition: Patient is asymptomatic after a significant SARS-CoV-2 exposure (COV-1 recommendations).

covid_urgent_therapy_despite_exposure.definition: Cancer-directed therapy is urgently required despite a significant SARS-CoV-2 exposure (COV-1 Table 1).

covid_persistent_context.definition: Context for persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection (COV-5). Persistent symptomatic infection with B-cell impairment is listed first.

high_risk_of_covid_progression.definition: High risk of COVID-19 disease progression within 7 days of symptom onset (COV-6 box). The box names no factors; the risk factors are those listed in the COV-3 box: prolonged neutropenia, T-cell deficiency, hematologic malignancy, tumor pulmonary involvement. Hematologic malignancy is taken from primary_disease (ALL, AML, MDS, lymphoma, multiple myeloma, CLL). Outpatient status is checked in the regimen rules.

hospitalized_with_symptomatic_covid.definition: Patient is hospitalized for acute symptomatic COVID-19 (COV-4 Antiviral Options box; also the 5-day remdesivir box in COV-6).

nirmatrelvir_dosing.definition: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir dosing by renal and hepatic function (COV-6).

molnupiravir_eligible.definition: Molnupiravir is an option (COV-6): outpatient, started within 5 days of symptom onset, and nirmatrelvir and remdesivir are both unavailable.

molnupiravir_fetal_risk_caution.definition: Molnupiravir fetal-harm caution applies: patient is pregnant or may become pregnant (COV-6).

notes.predicates: Conditions were drafted and reviewed by a language model (model_reviewed), not by clinicians. 'rejected' means the review rejected the draft; the box then needs clinician judgement. 'section_only' means the box only requires the patient to be in the page's guideline section.
notes.coordinates: bbox and line_bboxes are PDF points with the origin at the page's top left; pages[].size gives the page size.
notes.links: page links name a page id from pages[]; a multi-page code such as PROS-F has ids 'PROS-F 1 of 5' ... ; external_guideline links name another guideline's slug.
